sources.entry: icecream - Inspect variables, expressions, and program execution with a single, simple function call.

summary.one_liner: IceCream (ic) is a Python print-debugging helper that prints variable names with their values, execution context, and pretty-printed, syntax-highlighted output from a single function call.
summary.what_it_does: Calling ic(expr) prints the expression text alongside its value, so ic(foo(123)) shows "foo(123): 456". Calling ic() with no arguments prints the calling filename, line number, and parent function, which helps trace execution order. ic() returns its arguments, so it can be wrapped around existing code without changing behavior. ic.format() returns the output as a string instead of writing to stderr, and ic.disable()/ic.enable() turn output off and on. configureOutput() customizes the prefix, output function, argument-to-string function (with singledispatch registration for types such as numpy arrays), context inclusion, and absolute paths. install() makes ic available in builtins across all modules.
use_cases: trace which code branches run and in what order
log debug output with a custom prefix or logger
customize how specific types like numpy arrays are displayed while debugging
leave debug calls in code safely with a graceful fallback in production
notable: Prints the source text of the expression along with its value, not just the value
Argument-to-string conversion can be extended per type via functools.singledispatch register/unregister
Returns its arguments, so it can be inserted into existing code inline
install() exposes ic globally through the builtins module
Ports exist in many other languages (Dart, Rust, Go, Ruby, and more)
caveats: Output goes to stderr by default; formatting options are only as rich as the configureOutput settings described
Log-level integration is not built in; the README suggests combining ic.format() with logging as a workaround and calls this clunky
Targets Python 3 and PyPy3 only per the README
